verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left arm numbness, tingling, and weakness: "I can't quite move my left arm... it's numb, and then I also feel some, like tingling in my fingertips" and later agrees there is weakness rather than pain limitation: "it's not hurting, it's, like, numb, I can't feel it" and doctor summarizes as weakness.

Onset and progression described: "It's probably been, I'd say, for at least two weeks, and it's kind of gotten worse. Like,in the beginning, I just kind of felt a little bit of a tingling... and then it's gotten, it's gotten worse since then."

Distribution and rest symptoms: "I can feel it both in my, uh, um, you know a little bit in my elbow, and then in my arm, as well as in my hand"; digits: "it's my second, third, and fourth finger"; palmar side: "No. It's, it's the, it's this side. So, the front side."; at rest: "if i'm just like resting if I'm sitting like, right now, I can feel like it's numb, and I, I actually feel, tingling right now."

Piano difficulty and no glass-dropping, not pain-mediated: "I will say, um, well I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed it's been kind of harder to get the notes"; "So, have you been dropping things... have dropping it?" / "So not so much with the glass"; and "No, no, it's not hurting, it's not hurting, it's, like, numb, I can't feel it."

Shoulder pain with boxing movements: "sometimes I will feel it in my shoulder. Like if I try to, if I try to like you know move like in boxing and stuff, I will even like, uh, um, maybe feel a little bit of, a little bit of pain."

Tried nonpharmacologic measures without relief and ibuprofen use: "I tried to get a massage, it's not better. Or, you know, try to take warm baths. It's not better"; "I do take Ibuprofen because my muscles were sore... I kind of hurt like my knuckles on my right hand... so I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that."

Boxing class and flu-like illness after heavy drinking: "I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks"; illness: "I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago... we were like out partying until, you know, late hours, and I just got uncharacteristically drunk for me. And then after that, I was sick for probably good like two weeks... I think I must have had some kind of like a flu or something."

Transient partial left-eye vision loss: "I all of a sudden just couldn't see from the, uh, from my left eye. Like, I, I lost some, like a little bit of a field of vision... that just lasted maybe for, I don't know, twenty, twenty minutes?" and later "I think it was only maybe like twenty minutes or so... when I woke up it was gone."

Intermittent tired headaches and morning fatigue: "sometimes I get headaches but I think they're just tired headaches"; "sometimes like this morning for example, I just felt really, fatigued and I couldn't even get myself to the gym."

No seizures and normal legs/walking: "Ohh, no, no, no, no, nothing like that" in response to seizures/fits; "your weakness is only in your left arm. Legs are walking and all this, normal, yeah?" / "Right, exactly. Yeah, yeah, yeah, walking is normal, yeah."

As-needed ibuprofen: "I do take Ibuprofen because my muscles were sore... and... my knuckles on my right hand... so I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that." This indicates intermittent/as-needed use.

Vitamin D and poorly adhered iron supplements: "I just take ibuprofen every once in a while, I take vitamin D. Um, I take some I, I like my my GP really wants me to take iron supplements, but you know, they're just like huge pills so I, I, most of the time I just forget."
Melatonin use as needed: "But, vitamin D I take. And then, sometimes I take Melatonin to help me sleep."

No past medical history given: after being asked about past medical history, patient describes recent cold and visual issue and then says "but in general, I'm, I'm pretty healthy. You know, I work out, uh, , and I, I don't really have any medical problems." No chronic conditions are recorded.
Father’s conditions: "I know that my dad has I don't know if it it's hypo, I think it's hypothyroidism... he's got some autoimmune stuff going on, like that much I know."

Mother’s conditions: "my mom, my mom, she's actually not in a great shape. She's got diabetes type two. She's got hypertension, um, she's got, gosh, what is it, ohh, yeah, she's got high cholesterol." Hyperlipidemia = high cholesterol.
Exercise and boxing: "I work out" and "I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks."
Right-handed and plays piano: "I play a little bit of a piano" and "I can grasp a a glass but because I use my right hand most of the time, you know, I'm not left handed."
Heavy alcohol use, at least on one occasion: "we were like out partying until, you know, late hours, and I just got uncharacteristically drunk for me." This supports occasional heavy drinking.

Summary matches: "I can't quite move my left arm... it's numb... tingling" for ~2 weeks and worsening; not pain-limited: "it's not hurting, it's, like, numb". Doctor states concern for more than boxing and mentions MS/demyelinating disease: "sometimes you know you do get things like MS, multiple sclerosis... visual problems... numbness tingling sensations" and wants to investigate further. This aligns with concern for demyelinating process vs other etiology.

Doctor explicitly links visual disturbance and arm symptoms: "you said you can't, your vision went, your peripheral vision was not there for about twenty... and that with the weakness of the arms, make me think, is there something else going on rather than just an injury?" Visual episode was left eye, ~20 minutes, resolved as per patient.
Urgent neurology referral: "what we can do is I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral. Yeah?"

Potential brain imaging discussed: "What they, what that might entail is the brain scan and things like that." While MRI is not named, brain imaging is clearly planned; describing it as likely brain imaging with MRI is a standard direct clinical inference.

ED/A&E precautions: "while you're waiting for this to be done, if there's any weakness, uh, you know, if the weakness progresses to your legs, or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A and E."
